interactions.summary: Jiang opens the livestream from Beijing, thanks the Yale Beijing Center and the in-room and remote audience, invites chat questions, and frames Dante as a transformative encounter.
Carol Rafferty introduces Yale Center Beijing and frames the workshop as an attempt to pass on wisdom, beauty, light, truth, and the deepest human questions through Dante.

Jiang explains that the class will use a free online Divine Comedy resource, says the course will begin unusually with Paradise rather than Inferno, and asks students to share their written sense of heaven.

A facilitator prompts a student to speak into the microphone, and the student describes heaven as fulfillment, harmony, elevation beyond suffering, and a primarily felt rather than purely visual state.
interactions.speaker_attribution: Facilitator prompt followed by student answer

speaker_notes.note: The diarized speaker in seg-0007 is likely a room facilitator or Carol managing the microphone, not Jiang asking a substantive public question.

claims.claim: Jiang presents Dante as 'the greatest writer of all time' and frames the class as potentially life-transforming for participants.
claims.temporal_scope: Opening framing claim in the 2026-06-15 livestream.

claims.claim: The Divine Comedy is divided into Inferno, Purgatory, and Paradise.
Jiang deliberately starts the Dante workshop in Paradise, not at the beginning of the poem, and says the rationale will become clearer over time.
claims.temporal_scope: Method claim on 2026-06-15 for this two-week course.

claims.claim: The class will rely on a free shared website resource for reading and discussion throughout the two-week Dante workshop.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang begins not with modest orientation but with maximal stakes: Dante is the greatest writer, and the class could change your life.
signature_moments.source_phrase: dante is the greatest writer of all time
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It sets the public temperature of the series and tells later readers this Dante project is meant as existential formation, not literary housekeeping.

signature_moments.moment: The course opens in Paradise first, withholding the reason until the structure reveals itself.
signature_moments.source_phrase: we are gonna actually start in part 3
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It is Jiang's first methodological surprise and signals that sequence itself will become part of the interpretation.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The third part of Dante's Divine Comedy and the opening focus of this workshop.
Dante's three-part poem of Inferno, Purgatory, and Paradise, treated here as the central text of the course.

chronology_notes.note: This 2026-06-15 source is the opening session of a two-week Dante workshop livestreamed from Beijing and begins with Jiang's decision to enter the poem through Paradise.

uncertainty_notes.note: Carol's introduction contains noticeable ASR noise, so later public prose should preserve only the stable frame: Yale Center Beijing, wisdom beyond information, and the oldest human questions.
